name: Mental health assessment room
description: A calm, safe room in A&E where the mental health liaison team see patients in crisis once their body has been treated. Heavy fixed seats, nothing that can be thrown, a staff alarm strip and a second way out so nobody is ever trapped. The team aim to see everyone within an hour.
staffing: Hire a mental health nurse (or a psychiatrist) from Recruitment (H) to run it.

name: Section 136 suite
description: A place of safety for people the police have detained under Section 136 of the Mental Health Act. The police hand over here and get back on patrol, and the person waits in calm surroundings, not an A&E cubicle, for their Mental Health Act assessment. A low padded bed, heavy fixed seats, its own toilet, an observation window, a staff alarm strip and a second way out. Run by a mental health nurse.
staffing: Hire a mental health nurse from Recruitment (H) to run it.

name: Mental health ward
description: An adult mental health ward of single bedrooms, each with its own shower room. Patients stay a few days while they settle. Run by mental health nurses (one for every six beds), a psychiatrist and support workers, who stay with anyone on close observations. Nobody goes home until they are settled. Build a lounge and a garden nearby: time out of their rooms helps them settle.
staffing: Hire a mental health nurse for every 6 beds, a psychiatrist and a support worker for every 6 beds from Recruitment (H), posted to this ward. Other nurses and doctors can't work here.

name: Ward lounge
description: A homely lounge for the mental health wards: sofas, a television and a table for games and jigsaws. Patients come here by day to get out of their rooms, which helps them settle.
staffing: No staff of its own: the ward team look in on patients here.

name: Garden courtyard
description: A walled garden for the mental health wards, with raised planters, a tree and benches. On dry days patients sit out here for fresh air, which helps them settle more than anything else.
staffing: No staff of its own: the ward team look in on patients here.
